title: Image overlay
description: A standalone background layer: a pale bark-100 to needle-400 gradient with a decorative photograph (a real img from its CDN) laid over it in luminosity blend at one of three clarities (low, mid, high), and the photograph's credit at the bottom-left. It takes no children and never assumes the viewport: as the first child of a positioned container it fills that container's full width and height and sits behind the siblings that follow, so it can ground a whole screen, a card or a panel.

anatomy.description: Root div with data-slot="image-overlay": absolute, inset 0, width and height 100%, the bark-100 to needle-400 gradient (needle reached at 150%, so the ground stays pale; retuned 2026-09-28 from needle-400 into needle-700), isolated, an inline-size container named image-overlay, a flex box whose alignment (align-items end) seats the credit at the bottom-left. Accepts div props; `image` ({ url, creditHref, caption }) swaps the photograph and its credit together; `clarity` (low | mid | high, mid by default) sets how much of it shows. No children. Its module also sets, on any container holding it as a direct child, the lift pair at zero alpha and --control-hairline to pastel needle, so every neutral control on the ground is flat (theming §1.7, §4.6).

A decorative img (alt="", async decoding, high fetch priority) covering the ground at z-index -1 inside the isolated root: object-fit cover, luminosity blend, opacity by clarity (low 7.5%, mid 25%, high 50%; turned down 2026-09-28 with the paler ground), pointer-events none. An element, not a CSS url(): CSS cannot take a URL from a data attribute.

A p with a link to the photograph's page, placed bottom-left by the container's flex alignment (align-items end, 0.125rem 1rem padding): text-xs, bloom-950; bloom-200 on hover, the sidebar's outline step (--nav-outline) on focus.

usage: A background, not a wrapper: it takes no children. Render it as the first child of a positioned container (position: relative or absolute) and put the content after it; it fills the container's full width and height and the later siblings paint above it in DOM order.

It makes the ground busy and owns what that means for controls: the container holding it gets the lift turned off and a pastel needle hairline through the tokens, so an Input, Textarea or Select on it is flat with no prop (theming §4.6). The surface owns the override (§1.7); a busy ground without this layer sets the same three tokens in its own module.
It never assumes the viewport. The consumer owns the container, its position and its size: a full screen (min-height 100svh, as the login screen does), a card or a panel all work the same way.
Query narrow layouts against the consumer's container, not the overlay: declare container-type inline-size on the positioned container and write the queries on its children.
A sibling layout that covers the whole ground must give its bare areas pointer-events: none (and its columns pointer-events: auto), or the credit link beneath cannot be clicked.

Pass `image` to change the photograph and the credit changes with it; keep the licence satisfied through the caption. The default is an Unsplash photograph loaded from its CDN, so nothing ships in the bundle.

Keep the blend: luminosity takes the ground's green so the palette stays the only colour source. Pick clarity by what sits on it: low under copy on the ground, mid (default) under a card, high where the photograph is the point and nothing but a card's copy lands on it.
Do not hide the overlay from assistive tech: the credit is a real link and must stay reachable; the img already carries alt="".
Route code never styles the ground; a surface that needs a different ground is a variant here, not a rule in a route module.
